[package]
name = "horizon-mod-api-gen-tests"
version = "0.1.0"
edition.workspace = true
license.workspace = true
publish = false
description = "Generated mod API dispatch contract tests"

[dependencies]
serde_json = "1"

[build-dependencies]
horizon-mod-api-gen = { path = ".." }

[lints]
workspace = true

# Horizon APIs

Horizon has seven surfaces that other programs and people build on. Each one has an **API** (the contract: what you
may call, read or write, and what Horizon promises about it) and an **SDK** (the tools that help you use it). This
section has one page per surface, plus the rules every surface follows:
[stability and versioning](stability.md).

| Surface | For | API today | Stability | Reference |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Mods](../mods.md) | mod authors | content mods: manifest `api` 0.2; native mods: a horizon-mixins bundle ([native-mods.md](../native-mods.md)) | preview (content), experimental (native) | [mods.md](../mods.md) |
| [Shaders](shaders.md) | shader authors | API 0.1 (sky, vertex, material, weather and post stages, coloured block light, options, hot reload) | experimental | [shaders-reference.md](shaders-reference.md) |
| [Agent control](agent-control.md) | agents, scripts, tests | `horizon-ctl`, its MCP server, the game's control socket | preview | [horizon-ctl-commands.md](../horizon-ctl-commands.md) (generated) |
| [Servers](server.md) | hosts, panels, bots | `horizon-server` commands, `server.toml`, control API `/api/v1` | stable | [server-reference.md](server-reference.md) (generated) |
| [Launcher](launcher.md) | players' agents, pack makers | `horizon-launcher` commands and its MCP server | preview | [launcher-commands.md](../launcher-commands.md) (generated) |
| [Launch](launch.md) | other launchers | `horizon-client`'s launch options, the session JSON, exit codes; `horizon-prepare`'s output, `--check` and `--progress json` | experimental | [launch-reference.md](launch-reference.md) (generated) |
| [Data formats](data-formats.md) | tools that read Horizon's files | benchmark reports, telemetry, settings files, signed checksums | stable or preview, per format | on that page |

## How these APIs are designed

- **From the people who use them.** Each API starts from what a mod author, a pack author, a server host or an agent
  needs to do, written down as tasks ("a host backs up the world from a script"), and from how Horizon is built:
  Rust, wgpu and a server thread that runs every world. A function exists because a task
  needs it.
- **Our own design.** Horizon's APIs are not modelled on any other project's. Contributors may know other mod
  loaders, renderers and server platforms exist, but their source and API references are never read, copied or
  paraphrased here, and our names, shapes and docs are not taken from theirs. Vanilla Minecraft 26.3 is the reference for game
  concepts: ids, commands, `server.properties`, data packs and resource packs.
- **Safe by default.** A content mod is data and runs no code; a native mod runs with the player's rights, so it is
  off by default, behind a warning and reviewed before the registry lists it; the control
  sockets listen on this computer only, behind a token; nothing here is on by default where it would change vanilla's
  look or behaviour.
- **Free when unused.** An API nobody uses costs nothing per tick or per frame: no engine, no thread, no allocation.
- **One contract for every mode.** In-frame single player, the server thread, LAN and the dedicated server run the
  same gameplay code ([AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md)), so a server-side API serves all of them.

## References are generated

A reference page is written by code from the source it describes, and a test fails when the two differ:

| Page | Generated from | Update it with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [server-reference.md](server-reference.md) | `horizon-server`'s help, `config::TEMPLATE`, `api::ROUTES` | `HORIZON_WRITE_DOCS=1 cargo test -p horizon-server reference` |
| [horizon-ctl-commands.md](../horizon-ctl-commands.md) | the command table in `crates/horizon-client/src/bin/horizon-ctl/commands.rs` | `horizon-ctl help --markdown > docs/horizon-ctl-commands.md` |
| [launcher-commands.md](../launcher-commands.md) | `launcher/src/cli.rs` | `HORIZON_WRITE_DOCS=1 cargo test --manifest-path launcher/Cargo.toml the_launcher_reference` |
| [launch-reference.md](launch-reference.md) | `crates/horizon-client/src/game/launch_api.rs` | `HORIZON_WRITE_DOCS=1 cargo test -p horizon-client --lib launch_api` |

So a pull request that changes an API also changes its reference, and the reviewer sees the API's diff in the
reference's diff. The guides (overview, how-to, examples) are written by hand.

## Each surface's page

Every page has the same parts: **Overview** (what you can build), **Guide** (where to start), **Reference**,
**Examples**, **Stability** (the level of each part, per [stability.md](stability.md)), **Changelog** and
**Not there yet** (what is planned, so nobody builds on a guess).

The website shows these pages at [playhorizon.dev/docs/api](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/api), built from this
folder, and a summary for players and authors at [playhorizon.dev/docs/apis](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/apis)
(in the website's repository, horizon-rust/horizon-site).
The schema 1 sample read by `tests/schema.rs`; `tests/reference.rs` compiles its stages.

name: checks
# verify: every pull request and every push to main, on GitHub's runners (the repository is public). It is the
# check main requires, so it never has a condition: a skipped job counts as passed, and every run of this workflow
# must report a real verify (a pull request that changes no Rust finishes it in seconds instead).
# parity: the vanilla harnesses a pull request's changes can affect, on the Mac mini's runner, which holds the
# maintainer's own Minecraft files (Horizon never downloads the game); .github/workflows/parity.yml. Only for a pull
# request that changes a harness, oracle, probe or the runner: the rest are checked on main by parity-main. A fork's pull
# request runs it only when a maintainer adds the run-parity label (.github/workflows/run-parity.yml), so labels
# never start this workflow. See docs/release-flow.md.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
  workflow_dispatch:
permissions:
  contents: read
concurrency:
  # A new push to a pull request replaces its running checks; main's runs all finish (releases follow them).
  group: checks-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
env:
  # Test runs never reach the telemetry server: no live-count ping, no uploads (docs/telemetry.md).
  HORIZON_TELEMETRY_URL: "off"

jobs:
  # One job, not one per check: each job takes a runner from the organisation's shared pool, and with every pull request
  # and every merge to main starting this workflow, three jobs a run left the pool's queue tens of minutes deep.
  #
  # Where (docs/ci-runners.md): our checks runners (label horizon-checks: the desktop's, an isolated user, so a fork's
  # pull request runs there too) take the pull requests whose number ends in 0 or 1, about what their three runners
  # can do; GitHub's runners take the others and main's pushes (which also save the Rust cache GitHub's pull request
  # runs read), so both pools work at once. The repository variable SELF_HOSTED_CI moves them: `all` every job to
  # ours, `light` (the desktop paused) or `off` every job to GitHub's. On ours the build folder persists
  # (CARGO_TARGET_DIR, outside the checkout), so the apt packages, Python and the Rust cache steps are GitHub's only.
  verify:
    runs-on: >-
      ${{ vars.SELF_HOSTED_CI != 'off' && vars.SELF_HOSTED_CI != 'light' && (vars.SELF_HOSTED_CI == 'all' ||
      github.event_name == 'pull_request' && (endsWith(format('{0}', github.event.pull_request.number), '0') ||
      endsWith(format('{0}', github.event.pull_request.number), '1'))) &&
      fromJSON('["self-hosted", "linux", "horizon-checks"]') || 'ubuntu-latest' }}
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        if: runner.environment == 'github-hosted'
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'
      - name: Does this pull request need Rust checks?
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        id: rust
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: python3 tools/ci/rust_changes.py "$BASE_SHA" "$HEAD_SHA" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # A pull request adds only its own commits to main, so it reads those; main's pushes read every ref's history.
      - name: Keep game artifacts out of Git
        env:
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          python tools/check_public_tree.py
          if [ "$EVENT" = pull_request ]; then
            python tools/check_public_tree.py --range "$BASE_SHA..$HEAD_SHA"
          else
            python tools/check_public_tree.py --history
          fi
      # Our runners as GitHub's: some Python tests compile Rust with a bare `rustc` (GitHub's image has a default
      # toolchain, our runners' own rustup homes may not), and the GPU tests find no adapter there, so they return
      # early. Ours have Mesa's software Vulkan for parity; a backend Linux lacks keeps the tests from it, so a pull
      # request's verify doesn't depend on which pool took it (#8627: a GPU test that flakes on lavapipe).
      - name: Our runners as GitHub's (a default Rust toolchain, no GPU)
        if: runner.environment != 'github-hosted'
        run: |
          rustup toolchain install stable --profile minimal --component rustfmt --component clippy
          rustup default stable
          echo "WGPU_BACKEND=dx12" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - name: Test offline research tooling
        run: python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
      - name: Install Rust toolchain and the ALSA and udev headers the client links against
        if: steps.rust.outputs.required != 'false'
        env:
          HOSTED: ${{ runner.environment == 'github-hosted' }}
        run: |
          if [ "$HOSTED" = true ]; then
            sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends libasound2-dev libudev-dev
          fi
          rustup toolchain install stable --profile minimal --component rustfmt --component clippy
      # Dependencies and the workspace's own build, saved from main's runs (pull requests read main's cache).
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        if: steps.rust.outputs.required != 'false' && runner.environment == 'github-hosted'
        with:
          shared-key: verify
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
      - name: Check formatting and lint
        if: steps.rust.outputs.required != 'false'
        run: |
          cargo +stable fmt --all -- --check
          cargo +stable clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
          # The server build (released as horizon-engine): the game without sound or controllers.
          cargo +stable clippy -p horizon-client --all-targets --no-default-features -- -D warnings
      # Libraries, binaries and integration tests, then doc tests: not the ~275 examples, which clippy above already
      # type-checks and the parity job builds and runs (they were most of this step's build and link time).
      # cargo test, not nextest: nextest's process per test reloads each binary's shared tables for every test, and on
      # these 4-core runners it was no faster (#4978).
      - name: Test Rust core and voxel kernel correctness
        if: steps.rust.outputs.required != 'false'
        run: |
          cargo +stable test --workspace --lib --bins --tests
          # The full content-root tests (#[ignore]d: minutes each on a laptop). The same build as above; they need the
          # prepared vanilla data, so without it they pass at once. Keep the target selection identical to avoid
          # recompiling the workspace with a different dependency graph.
          cargo +stable test --workspace --lib --bins --tests mod_content::tests:: -- --ignored
          cargo +stable test --workspace --doc
  # The launcher is its own workspace (launcher/Cargo.toml), so verify's cargo runs never build it. A pull request that
  # changes it or a crate it builds is checked here, and so is every push to main: two pull requests can each pass
  # alone and break it together (#2059 and the registry ratings did, 2026-10-26).
  launcher:
    runs-on: >-
      ${{ vars.SELF_HOSTED_CI != 'off' && vars.SELF_HOSTED_CI != 'light' && (vars.SELF_HOSTED_CI == 'all' ||
      github.event_name == 'pull_request' && (endsWith(format('{0}', github.event.pull_request.number), '0') ||
      endsWith(format('{0}', github.event.pull_request.number), '1'))) &&
      fromJSON('["self-hosted", "linux", "horizon-checks"]') || 'ubuntu-latest' }}
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Does this pull request change the launcher or a crate it builds?
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        id: launcher
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: python3 tools/ci/rust_changes.py --launcher "$BASE_SHA" "$HEAD_SHA" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Install Rust and the headers GPUI links against
        if: steps.launcher.outputs.required != 'false'
        env:
          HOSTED: ${{ runner.environment == 'github-hosted' }}
        run: |
          if [ "$HOSTED" = true ]; then
            sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends libxkbcommon-x11-dev libwayland-dev \
              libx11-xcb-dev libfontconfig-dev libvulkan-dev libasound2-dev libudev-dev
          fi
          rustup toolchain install stable --profile minimal --component rustfmt --component clippy
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        if: steps.launcher.outputs.required != 'false' && runner.environment == 'github-hosted'
        with:
          workspaces: launcher
          shared-key: launcher
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
      - name: Check the launcher's formatting, lint and tests
        if: steps.launcher.outputs.required != 'false'
        working-directory: launcher
        run: |
          cargo +stable fmt --check
          cargo +stable clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
          cargo +stable test --locked --lib
  # Compile and test Windows ARM64 on an actual ARM64 host, and inspect the resulting PE headers. By hand only
  # (`gh workflow run checks --ref <branch>`): GitHub's runner queue is the bottleneck, and main's runs gate the
  # releases (tools/release_train.py waits for them), so neither pull requests nor main's pushes start this
  # 90-minute job. The Nightly and launcher releases build and check these binaries on every run.
  windows-arm64:
    name: Windows ARM64 game and launcher
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    runs-on: windows-11-vs2026-arm
    timeout-minutes: 90
    env:
      RUSTFLAGS: -C target-feature=+crt-static
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Use every runner core for Cargo
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $cores = (Get-CimInstance Win32_Processor | Measure-Object -Property NumberOfLogicalProcessors -Sum).Sum
          "CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=$cores" >> $env:GITHUB_ENV
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: aarch64-pc-windows-msvc
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          shared-key: windows-arm64-game
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: launcher
          shared-key: windows-arm64-launcher
      - name: Check LLVM assembler used by ring
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $llvmBin = Join-Path $env:ProgramFiles 'LLVM\bin'
          if (-not (Get-Command clang -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) -and (Test-Path (Join-Path $llvmBin 'clang.exe'))) {
            $env:PATH = "$llvmBin;$env:PATH"
            "PATH=$env:PATH" >> $env:GITHUB_ENV
          }
          $clang = Get-Command clang -ErrorAction Stop
          Write-Output "Using $($clang.Source)"
          & $clang.Source --version
      - name: Build the game for native Windows ARM64
        run: cargo build --release --locked --target aarch64-pc-windows-msvc -p horizon-client -p horizon-client-lib --bin horizon-client --bin horizon-ctl -p horizon-prepare --bin horizon-prepare -p horizon-server --bin horizon-server
      - name: Check the game's PE machine
        run: python tools/check_pe_arch.py arm64 target/aarch64-pc-windows-msvc/release/horizon-client.exe target/aarch64-pc-windows-msvc/release/horizon-ctl.exe target/aarch64-pc-windows-msvc/release/horizon-prepare.exe target/aarch64-pc-windows-msvc/release/horizon-server.exe
      - name: Check game DLL imports
        run: python tools/check_imports.py target/aarch64-pc-windows-msvc/release/horizon-client.exe target/aarch64-pc-windows-msvc/release/horizon-ctl.exe target/aarch64-pc-windows-msvc/release/horizon-prepare.exe target/aarch64-pc-windows-msvc/release/horizon-server.exe
      - name: Start every game executable
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
          $client = 'target/aarch64-pc-windows-msvc/release/horizon-client.exe'
          $output = & $client --help 2>&1
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or ($output -join "`n") -notmatch '--resources') { throw 'horizon-client --help failed' }
          foreach ($binary in @('horizon-ctl.exe', 'horizon-prepare.exe', 'horizon-server.exe')) {
            $path = "target/aarch64-pc-windows-msvc/release/$binary"
            $output = & $path --help 2>&1
            if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or -not $output) { throw "$binary --help failed" }
          }
          foreach ($binary in @('horizon-prepare.exe', 'horizon-server.exe')) {
            $path = "target/aarch64-pc-windows-msvc/release/$binary"
            $output = & $path --version 2>&1
            if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or -not $output) { throw "$binary --version failed" }
            Write-Output ($output -join "`n")
          }
      - name: Test and build the native Windows ARM64 launcher
        working-directory: launcher
        run: |
          cargo test --release --locked --target aarch64-pc-windows-msvc --lib
          cargo build --release --locked --target aarch64-pc-windows-msvc
      - name: Check the launcher's PE machine
        working-directory: launcher
        run: python ../tools/check_pe_arch.py arm64 target/aarch64-pc-windows-msvc/release/horizon-launcher.exe
      - name: Check launcher DLL imports and command-line startup
        working-directory: launcher
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
          $launcher = 'target/aarch64-pc-windows-msvc/release/horizon-launcher.exe'
          python ../tools/check_imports.py $launcher
          $output = & $launcher --version 2>&1
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or -not $output) { throw 'horizon-launcher --version failed' }
          Write-Output ($output -join "`n")
  # Most pull requests leave the harnesses to parity-main, which runs them on main a batch of merges at a time
  # (.github/workflows/parity-main.yml; releases wait for it). A pull request still runs them itself when it changes
  # a harness, an oracle, a probe or the runner, or carries the run-parity label (run-parity.yml, when it is added).
  parity-scope:
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    # A git diff of this repository's own branch: one of our small runners (horizon-light, docs/ci-runners.md).
    runs-on: ${{ vars.SELF_HOSTED_CI != 'off' && fromJSON('["self-hosted", "linux", "horizon-light"]') || 'ubuntu-latest' }}
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: scope
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          LABELS: ${{ join(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, ' ') }}
        run: |
          changed=$(git diff --name-only "$(git merge-base "$BASE_SHA" HEAD)" HEAD)
          harness=$(grep -E '^(tools/test_[a-z0-9_]+_parity\.py|tools/(parity[a-z_]*|lab)\.py|tools/parity_hosts\.json|mods/horizon/src/test/|crates/[^/]+/examples/|crates/horizon-client/src/game/[a-z_]*(fixture|harness)\.rs|\.github/workflows/parity[a-z-]*\.yml)' <<< "$changed" || true)
          if [ -n "$harness" ] || [[ " $LABELS " == *" run-parity "* ]]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "The pull request runs its harnesses: ${harness:-label run-parity}"
          else
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "No harness, oracle, probe or runner change: parity-main checks this on main"
          fi
  parity:
    needs: parity-scope
    if: needs.parity-scope.outputs.run == 'true'
    uses: ./.github/workflows/parity.yml
    with:
      base: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
      head: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
      full: ${{ contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'full-parity') }}
  # Horizon never downloads the game. These jobs need a self-hosted Linux runner
  # (label horizon-game) holding the maintainer's own copy: the official launcher's
  # game directory in HORIZON_MINECRAFT_DIR and the pinned server jar in
  # HORIZON_SERVER_JAR. Start them by hand: gh workflow run checks --ref <branch>.
  vanilla-parity:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    runs-on: [self-hosted, linux, horizon-game]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'
      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        run: rustup toolchain install stable --profile minimal
      - uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '25'
      - name: Compare Rust foundations with pinned vanilla client and server bytecode
        env:
          RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: stable
        run: python tools/test_rust_parity.py --prepare
      - name: Check Rust world-data interoperability with pinned vanilla client and server
        env:
          RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: stable
        run: python tools/test_world_parity.py
      - name: Compare scheduled ticks and saved tick data with pinned vanilla client and server
        env:
          RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: stable
        run: python tools/test_tick_parity.py
      - name: Compare simulation geometry and cached block collision shapes
        env:
          RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: stable
        run: |
          python tools/test_geometry_parity.py
          python tools/test_collision_parity.py
      - name: Compare noise samplers and density kernels with pinned vanilla client and server
        env:
          RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: stable
        run: python tools/test_noise_parity.py
      - name: Compare compiled density samplers with pinned vanilla client and server
        env:
          RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: stable
        run: python tools/test_density_parity.py
      - name: Compare world-generation JSON codecs with pinned vanilla client and server
        env:
          RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: stable
        run: python tools/test_worldgen_parity.py
      - name: Compare heightmap predicates and chunk mutations with pinned vanilla client and server
        env:
          RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: stable
        run: python tools/test_heightmap_parity.py
      - name: Compare pre-light chunk status transitions and block writes
        env:
          RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: stable
        run: python tools/test_chunk_stage_parity.py
      - name: Compare feature placement into resident neighboring chunks
        env:
          RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: stable
        run: python tools/test_feature_region_parity.py
      - name: Compare nested feature selectors and sequences
        env:
          RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: stable
        run: python tools/test_feature_graph_parity.py
      - name: Compare named feature holders and placed-feature tags
        env:
          RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: stable
        run: python tools/test_feature_catalog_parity.py
      - name: Compare configured fill-layer block placement
        env:
          RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: stable
        run: python tools/test_fill_layer_parity.py
      - name: Compare replacement-rule codecs and evaluation
        env:
          RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: stable
        run: python tools/test_rule_test_parity.py
      - name: Compare simple-block placement and feature composition
        env:
          RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: stable
        run: python tools/test_simple_block_parity.py
      - name: Compare block-column sampling and obstruction
        env:
          RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: stable
        run: python tools/test_block_column_parity.py
      - name: Compare vertical pillars and cap feature placement
        env:
          RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: stable
        run: python tools/test_pillar_parity.py
      - name: Compare exactly-one-neighbor feature spreading
        env:
          RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: stable
        run: python tools/test_neighbor_spread_parity.py
      - name: Compare block-pile support and placement
        env:
          RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: stable
        run: python tools/test_block_pile_parity.py
      - name: Compare disk replacement and postprocessing
        env:
          RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: stable
        run: python tools/test_disk_parity.py
      - name: Compare block-blob support search and geometry
        env:
          RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: stable
        run: python tools/test_block_blob_parity.py
      - name: Compare spring placement and fluid tick scheduling
        env:
          RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: stable
        run: python tools/test_spring_parity.py
      - name: Compare vine attachment priority and placement
        env:
          RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: stable
        run: python tools/test_vines_parity.py
      - name: Compare underwater magma floor scans and occlusion
        env:
          RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: stable
        run: python tools/test_underwater_magma_parity.py

"""Runs tests/install_sh_signature.sh: packaging/server/install.sh checks the release signature.

PURPOSE: keep install.sh's Ed25519 check from regressing (docs/release-flow.md, "Signed checksums").
REFS: tests/install_sh_signature.sh, tools/ci/sign_release.sh.
Skips quietly on Windows and without bash or OpenSSL 3. Headless, no network.
"""

import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

SCRIPT = Path(__file__).with_name("install_sh_signature.sh")


class InstallShSignature(unittest.TestCase):
    # install.sh installs the Linux and macOS server and refuses anything else, and a bare "bash" on Windows is
    # System32's WSL one (#5383), which can't see the host's paths.
    @unittest.skipIf(os.name == "nt", "install.sh is for Linux and macOS")
    @unittest.skipUnless(shutil.which("bash") and shutil.which("openssl"), "bash and openssl needed")
    def test_signature_cases(self):
        run = subprocess.run(["bash", str(SCRIPT)], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=300)
        if run.returncode == 77:
            self.skipTest(run.stdout.strip())
        self.assertEqual(run.returncode, 0, run.stdout + run.stderr)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

#!/bin/bash
# PURPOSE: proves packaging/server/install.sh checks the release signature (docs/release-flow.md, "Signed checksums").
# WHY: the first install used to trust only the SHA-256 GitHub publishes (docs/security.md).
# REFS: tools/ci/sign_release.sh (signs the fake releases with a throwaway key), crates/horizon-release-sign.
# LOGS: prints one ok/FAIL line per case; exit 1 when any case fails.
# READS-BY: tests/test_install_sh_signature.py (unittest wrapper), by hand: bash tests/install_sh_signature.sh
# ENDS-WHEN: it ends by itself; leaves nothing outside its own mktemp folder.
# Needs OpenSSL 3 (to sign the throwaway release); skips (exit 77) without it. curl is replaced by a fake that
# serves local files, so nothing touches the network.
set -u
root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
openssl version | grep -Eq '^OpenSSL [3-9]\.' || { echo "skip: OpenSSL 3 needed"; exit 77; }
W=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$W"' EXIT
fails=0
check() {  # name, expected exit (0 or 1), output grep (may be empty), then the case's exit and output files
  local name=$1 want=$2 pat=$3 rc=$4 out=$5
  local exit_ok=no
  if [ "$want" = 0 ]; then [ "$rc" = 0 ] && exit_ok=yes; else [ "$rc" != 0 ] && exit_ok=yes; fi
  if [ "$exit_ok" = yes ] && { [ -z "$pat" ] || grep -q -- "$pat" "$out"; }; then
    echo "ok   $name"
  else echo "FAIL $name (exit $rc, wanted $want, pattern '$pat')"; sed 's/^/     /' "$out"; fails=$((fails+1)); fi
}

# A fake release: an archive holding horizon-server, signed for TAG with a throwaway key.
make_release() {  # dir tag
  local d=$1 tag=$2
  mkdir -p "$d/src/horizon-server-x" "$d/files"
  printf '#!/bin/sh\necho fake\n' > "$d/src/horizon-server-x/horizon-server"; chmod +x "$d/src/horizon-server-x/horizon-server"
  tar -czf "$d/files/horizon-server-linux-x86_64.tar.gz" -C "$d/src" horizon-server-x
  EPHEMERAL=yes bash "$root/tools/ci/sign_release.sh" "$tag" "$d/files/horizon-server-linux-x86_64.tar.gz" > /dev/null
  json "$d" "$tag" yes
}
json() {  # dir tag with-sums: GitHub's release JSON, as install.sh reads it
  local d=$1 tag=$2 sums=$3 sha
  sha=$(sha256sum "$d/files/horizon-server-linux-x86_64.tar.gz" | cut -d' ' -f1)
  {
    printf '{\n  "tag_name": "%s",\n  "name": "%s",\n  "assets": [\n' "$tag" "$tag"
    printf '    {\n      "name": "horizon-server-linux-x86_64.tar.gz",\n      "digest": "sha256:%s",\n      "browser_download_url": "https://dl.test/horizon-server-linux-x86_64.tar.gz"\n    }' "$sha"
    if [ "$sums" = yes ]; then for f in SHA256SUMS SHA256SUMS.sig; do
      printf ',\n    {\n      "name": "%s",\n      "browser_download_url": "https://dl.test/%s"\n    }' "$f" "$f"; done; fi
    printf '\n  ]\n}\n'
  } > "$d/release.json"
}
# Tools install.sh may use, without openssl (the "no OpenSSL" case).
mkdir "$W/nossl"
for t in sh bash cat awk sed grep cut head find mkdir mktemp rm mv ln chmod cp basename dirname tar gzip sha256sum ls uname printf; do
  p=$(command -v "$t") && ln -s "$p" "$W/nossl/$t"
done
# The fake curl: the API address answers with release.json, any other address with the file of that name.
mkdir "$W/fake"
cat > "$W/fake/curl" <<'CURL'
#!/bin/sh
out=; url=
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do case "$1" in -o) out=$2; shift 2 ;; -*) shift ;; *) url=$1; shift ;; esac; done
case "$url" in
  https://api.github.com/*) src=$REL/release.json ;;
  *) src=$REL/files/$(basename "$url") ;;
esac
[ -f "$src" ] || exit 22
if [ -n "$out" ]; then cp "$src" "$out"; else cat "$src"; fi
CURL
chmod +x "$W/fake/curl"

# install.sh with the throwaway public key in place of the release key.
with_key() {  # dir -> prints path of the patched copy
  local d=$1
  sed "s|^RELEASE_KEYS=.*|RELEASE_KEYS=\"$(cat "$d/files/ephemeral.pub")\"|" "$root/packaging/server/install.sh" > "$d/install.sh"
  grep -q "$(cat "$d/files/ephemeral.pub")" "$d/install.sh" || { echo "FAIL could not set the test key"; exit 1; }
}
run() {  # dir, path-dir, ...install args: runs the patched install.sh with fake curl
  local d=$1 p=$2; shift 2
  REL=$d PATH="$W/fake:$p" HOME="$W/home" sh "$d/install.sh" --dir "$d/inst" --bin "$d/bin" "$@" > "$d/out" 2>&1
  echo $? > "$d/rc"
}
case_run() { run "$@"; }
verdict() { check "$1" "$2" "$3" "$(cat "$4/rc")" "$4/out"; }
# sed -i differs between GNU and BSD (macOS) sed: edit through a copy instead.
edit() {  # sed-expression file
  sed "$1" "$2" > "$2.tmp" && mv "$2.tmp" "$2"
}
mkdir -p "$W/home"
P=/usr/bin:/bin

# 1. Good signature, a Nightly (signed for the channel "nightly" under the tag nightly-2026-11-03).
d=$W/good; make_release "$d" nightly; with_key "$d"
edit 's/"tag_name": "nightly"/"tag_name": "nightly-2026-11-03"/' "$d/release.json"
run "$d" "$P"; verdict "good signature installs (nightly channel)" 0 "Release signature OK" "$d"
[ -x "$d/inst/current/horizon-server" ] || { echo "FAIL nothing installed"; fails=$((fails+1)); }

# 2. Good signature, a normal tag.
d=$W/tag; make_release "$d" v1.2.3; with_key "$d"
run "$d" "$P" --version v1.2.3; verdict "good signature installs (release tag)" 0 "Release signature OK" "$d"

# 3. Tampered archive: GitHub's digest is made to agree with the swapped archive, only SHA256SUMS catches it.
d=$W/arc; make_release "$d" v1.2.3; with_key "$d"
printf 'x' >> "$d/files/horizon-server-linux-x86_64.tar.gz"; json "$d" v1.2.3 yes
run "$d" "$P" --version v1.2.3; verdict "tampered archive refused" 1 "doesn't match its SHA-256" "$d"
[ ! -e "$d/inst/current" ] || { echo "FAIL tampered archive was installed"; fails=$((fails+1)); }

# 4. Tampered SHA256SUMS (the archive's line swapped for the hash of the tampered archive).
d=$W/sums; make_release "$d" v1.2.3; with_key "$d"
printf 'x' >> "$d/files/horizon-server-linux-x86_64.tar.gz"
new=$(sha256sum "$d/files/horizon-server-linux-x86_64.tar.gz" | cut -d' ' -f1)
printf '%s  horizon-server-linux-x86_64.tar.gz\n' "$new" > "$d/files/SHA256SUMS"; json "$d" v1.2.3 yes
run "$d" "$P" --version v1.2.3; verdict "tampered SHA256SUMS refused" 1 "signature doesn't match" "$d"

# 5. A signature made for another tag does not pass (a release's list replayed under another tag).
d=$W/replay; make_release "$d" v1.2.3; with_key "$d"
edit 's/"tag_name": "v1.2.3"/"tag_name": "v9.9.9"/' "$d/release.json"
run "$d" "$P" --version v9.9.9; verdict "signature replayed under another tag refused" 1 "signature doesn't match" "$d"

# 6. Signed by a key that is not the release key.
d=$W/wrong; make_release "$d" v1.2.3; with_key "$d"
edit 's|^RELEASE_KEYS=.*|RELEASE_KEYS="MU4oiIQcCxkZvbwSjjXs7SySCuM6ywRQ3nGaJYZG0gw="|' "$d/install.sh"
run "$d" "$P" --version v1.2.3; verdict "wrong key refused" 1 "signature doesn't match" "$d"

# 7. No OpenSSL: says so, keeps the SHA-256 check.
d=$W/none; make_release "$d" v1.2.3; with_key "$d"
run "$d" "$W/nossl" --version v1.2.3; verdict "no OpenSSL: installs, says it was not checked" 0 "OpenSSL isn't installed" "$d"
printf 'x' >> "$d/files/horizon-server-linux-x86_64.tar.gz"
d2=$W/none2; cp -r "$d" "$d2"; rm -rf "$d2/inst" "$d2/bin"; edit 's/"digest": "sha256:[0-9a-f]*"/"digest": "sha256:0000"/' "$d2/release.json"
run "$d2" "$W/nossl" --version v1.2.3; verdict "no OpenSSL: a wrong GitHub SHA-256 still refused" 1 "doesn't match its SHA-256" "$d2"

# 8. Old OpenSSL and LibreSSL (macOS): says so, keeps the SHA-256 check.
for v in "OpenSSL 1.1.1w  11 Sep 2023" "LibreSSL 3.3.6"; do
  d=$W/old; rm -rf "$d"; make_release "$d" v1.2.3; with_key "$d"
  mkdir -p "$W/old-bin"; rm -f "$W/old-bin/openssl"
  printf '#!/bin/sh\necho "%s"\n' "$v" > "$W/old-bin/openssl"; chmod +x "$W/old-bin/openssl"
  REL=$d PATH="$W/old-bin:$W/fake:$W/nossl" HOME="$W/home" sh "$d/install.sh" --dir "$d/inst" --bin "$d/bin" --version v1.2.3 > "$d/out" 2>&1; echo $? > "$d/rc"
  verdict "${v%% *}: installs, says it can't check signatures" 0 "can't check Ed25519" "$d"
done

# 9. A release published before signing (no SHA256SUMS): says so, keeps the SHA-256 check.
d=$W/legacy; make_release "$d" v1.2.3; with_key "$d"; json "$d" v1.2.3 no
run "$d" "$P" --version v1.2.3; verdict "unsigned release: installs, says so" 0 "no signed checksums" "$d"

echo "$fails case(s) failed"; [ "$fails" = 0 ]

        for velocity in ([0.0, 0.0, 0.0], [0.125, -0.0625, -0.25], [-1.0, 0.5, 0.75]):
            for owned in ([False], [True], [True, False], [True, False, True],
                          [False, True, True], [True, True, False, False, True]):
                out.append(dict(name=f'authority-{len(out)}', spin=spin, velocity=velocity, owned=owned))
    # A rider who leaves while the boat is moving, sits out long enough for the
    # empty boat to stop, and boards again (#6589): the re-boarded boat must
    # keep the velocity it had while empty, not the one the rider left with.
    for spin in (0.0, 0.125, -17.0):
        for velocity in ([1.0, 0.25, -0.5], [-0.125, 0.0, 0.0625]):
            for empty in (5, 25, 60):

                    owned = [True] * 8 + [False] + [False] * empty + [True] * back
                    out.append(dict(name=f'reboard-{len(out)}', spin=spin, velocity=velocity, owned=owned))
            # Empty from the first tick, then boarded: the boat has only ever
            # moved while nobody rode it.
            out.append(dict(name=f'reboard-{len(out)}', spin=spin, velocity=velocity,

                                    timeout=900)

    run(['javac', '--release', lock['minecraft']['java_major'], '-proc:none', '-nowarn',
         '-sourcepath', sources, '-cp', dependencies, '-d', classes,

        'compile-java')
    run(['java', '-cp', str(classes) + os.pathsep + dependencies, 'dev.horizonlab.parity.VanillaBoatAuthorityOracle',

# Entity model document loading

The three startup batches (boats/chest boats, minecarts, armor stands/player armor)
now share one parsed document. For this fixture, that replaces 43 full document
reads/parses (boat discovery plus 42 selected layers) with one. Selected models
still produce independent `Part` trees; the document is dropped after the batches
are built. Other entity loaders retain their existing behavior.

## Reproduce

From the repository root:

```sh
python3 benchmarks/entity-model-document-2026-10-14/generate_fixture.py /tmp/horizon-entity-model-document-fixture.json
ENTITY_MODEL_BENCH_DOCUMENT=/tmp/horizon-entity-model-document-fixture.json \
  CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/bob/Documents/horizon/target \
  cargo test -p horizon-client --profile fast --bin horizon-client \
  entity_model_document_benchmark -- --ignored --nocapture
```

`CARGO_TARGET_DIR` is optional and can be changed for another machine. Supply a
prepared `entity-models.json` through `ENTITY_MODEL_BENCH_DOCUMENT` to benchmark
that document instead; the harness copies only that file to a temporary root.
`ENTITY_MODEL_BENCH_REPETITIONS` controls repetitions (default 15).

The opt-in Rust test calls the actual three optimized production loaders and
compares every selected part name, pose, polygon normal/vertex and child against
the previous algorithm using the compatible per-model `load_model` API. Timings
include reading, parsing, constructing, normalizing into a common result map, and
dropping the result. Each variant gets three warmups and 15 measured calls, with
order alternating. `black_box` consumes inputs/results. No other builds or
optimization benchmarks ran during the measured calls.

## Input and limitations

Prepared resources were unavailable in the repository and local Horizon asset
directories. This is a **synthetic** 2,473,695-byte document with 458 model layers,
each containing 12 posed parts with six exported quads and normals. It selects 22
boat/chest-boat layers, six minecart layers and 14 armor/player layers (42 total).
One wood name is synthetic (`test_wood`); boat discovery accepts arbitrary wood
names. The extra layers model the cost of parsing a full production-size document
for each selected model.

File data is warm in the OS page cache. Equipment files are absent, so equipment
texture loading is excluded. This measures the entity-model batch only and does
not establish overall startup, frame time or FPS improvement. Shapes/layer counts
in real prepared documents can produce different absolute timings.

Machine: AMD Ryzen 5 5600X (6 cores / 12 threads), Linux x86_64,
Rust 1.99.0 (b940084d7, LLVM 23.1.1), Cargo `fast` profile (opt-level 3,
16 codegen units, no LTO). Baseline algorithm corresponds to main
`73a019967e9665c6b96332988c13cb66679d8477`.

## Results

| Variant | Median batch time | Full document reads/parses |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Previous per-model algorithm | 1,434.974 ms | 43 |
| Shared document | 33.420 ms | 1 |

The measured batch is **42.94× faster** on this synthetic input. All 15 samples
for both variants, warmup count, document size and selected model count are in
[`results.json`](results.json).

## Validation

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/bob/Documents/horizon/target \
  cargo test -p horizon-client --profile fast --bin horizon-client \
  entity_model_loading_tests -- --nocapture
CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/bob/Documents/horizon/target \
  cargo clippy -p horizon-client --profile fast --lib --bin horizon-client --tests -- -D warnings
```

The regular tests cover full/sparse documents, unrelated layers, a missing file,
invalid JSON, non-object JSON, missing model keys, independent model trees, and
equipment loading when the document is unavailable.
